title: Ikrimah, son of Abu Jahl
hookLine: son of Abu Jahl, forgiven and welcomed, and his father not to be insulted in front of him (sirah)

cards: Some names are hard to carry. Abu Jahl, father of ignorance, is the name tradition says the Muslims gave a leading enemy of the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, in Mecca.
The biographies say he fell at Badr, and that his son Ikrimah kept fighting after him. When Mecca opened and others were given safety, Ikrimah ran, south toward Yemen and the sea.
A man with his father's name hanging over him, and every reason to think there is no way back. Today: what happened when he came back anyway.

teach.b: The biographies tell it this way. Ikrimah's wife, Umm Hakim, stayed in Mecca and became Muslim. She asked the Prophet for safety for her husband, and it was given.
Then she went after him herself, all the way to the coast, and brought him home.
One report adds a storm at sea, when the sailors told everyone aboard to call on God alone, and Ikrimah thought: if only God can save me at sea, only God can save me on land.
A version of that scene is kept in Sunan an-Nasa'i, not in Bukhari. Before Ikrimah reached the city, the biographies say, the Prophet told his companions: Ikrimah is coming to you as a believer.
Do not insult his father, because insulting the dead hurts the living and does not reach the dead. People had plenty of stories about Abu Jahl. The instruction was: not in front of his son.
A report in Tirmidhi, from Ikrimah himself, gives the greeting he got: welcome to the rider, the emigrant. Not the son of the enemy.
A traveler in from the road, greeted at the door. The same respect for the dead runs through a hadith in Bukhari, from Aisha: do not abuse the dead, for they have gone on to what they sent ahead.

how: Muslims are taught not to speak ill of the dead, and Ikrimah's story is told as an example of welcoming someone back without shaming them for their family.

games.q: you're a companion. Ikrimah, son of a leading enemy of the Prophet, is about to walk in as a believer. people have plenty to say about his father. what are you told?
o: say what you like; it's all true.
don't insult his father in front of him.
make him answer for his father first.
games.why: the biographies say the Prophet told them not to insult his father: it hurts the living and does not reach the dead.

practice: Think of someone whose mother or father is hard to like, a friend's difficult dad, a public figure, maybe a parent of your own, and notice the stories you usually tell about that person.
Let them stay untold; you're not pretending the past was fine, you're sparing the living. If you pray, you can ask mercy for the parents of the people around you.

wordCard.voice: Ikrimah. Son of Abu Jahl, who fled when Mecca opened, was brought back by his wife, and was greeted at the door as a rider and an emigrant, with his father's name kept off people's lips. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: welcome; the word of the greeting Ikrimah reports he was given.

carryVoice: Your line: welcomed like a traveler. His father's name stayed outside the door. Day eight hundred forty-five, done.
